hypotheses.justification: Lean can already infer this instance from `[CartesianMonoidalCategory K]`. Mathlib's `Monoidal/Cartesian/Basic.lean` (line 505) has `instance (priority := 100) : Limits.HasFiniteProducts C` for any cartesian monoidal category; it is built from `tensorProductIsBinaryProduct`. `HasBinaryProducts K` is an `abbrev` for `HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) K`. The instance `hasLimitsOfShape_discrete [HasFiniteProducts C] (ι) [Finite ι]` in `Limits/Shapes/FiniteProducts.lean` supplies it for the finite type `WalkingPair`. So if the binder is dropped (`omit [HasBinaryProducts K] in`), the statement still elaborates: `tensorLeftIsoProd A`, which takes `[HasBinaryProducts C]`, and `prod.fst` both get the inferred instance. The proof is unchanged and works for any instance: `(tensorProductIsBinaryProduct A B).conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp (limit.isLimit _) ⟨.left⟩` only uses `limit.isLimit` for whatever `HasLimit (pair A B)` instance is in use, and `tensorLeftIsoProd` is defined by that same `conePointUniqueUpToIso`. The statement is a special case of the original theorem, with the binder filled by the inferred instance, so it remains true. The library's own uses of `tensorLeftIsoProd` for presheaf categories `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w` already rely on instance inference in the same way. I checked the instance in Mathlib master, not in the version the library pins.
